title: Version audit
briefing: A security bulletin lands: a bug affects some OpenSSL builds. Before you can
tell whether app-01 is exposed, you need to know exactly which version of
dpkg is the fastest way to answer 'what version is installed?'.
tips: `dpkg -l openssl` (or `dpkg -s openssl`) prints the installed version.
Record the upstream version — the 3.x.y part at the front.
objective: Find the installed openssl package version and write its upstream number (the 3.x.y part) to ~/openssl.txt.
expert_objective: Record app-01's installed openssl version in ~/openssl.txt.
hints: Query it: `dpkg -l openssl`. The Version column shows 3.0.11-1~deb12u2.
The upstream version is the leading 3.0.11. Write it to the file.
explanation: Patch management starts with 'what do we actually run?'. `dpkg -l <pkg>` (or `dpkg -s`) gives the exact installed version — the number you compare against a CVE's 'fixed in' line to decide if a box needs updating.
